extracted.intended_audience: Researchers who perform and report in vivo (animal) experiments; journal editors and peer reviewers assessing animal research reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for what to include when reporting in vivo animal experiments (ARRIVE 2.0), giving a prioritized set of items (Essential 10) plus a Recommended Set; intended to improve transparency, reproducibility and assessment of reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design (1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, provide brief details of study design including the groups being compared and the experimental unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report groups being compared (including control groups or rationale if none used). Explain choice of negative/positive/comparator controls relevant to the objective. For complex designs provide a visual representation (timeline diagram or flow chart) to show which treatments/procedures applied to which animals and when. Avoid selective reporting or excluding experimental groups because data conflict with the narrative. State if the same control group was used for multiple experiments or if no control was used. Use design tools (e.g. Experimental Design Assistant) for diagramming complex features (crossed/nested factors, blocking, repeated measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: The groups being compared (1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The groups being compared, including control groups. If no control group has been used, the rationale should be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative controls determine whether differences are caused by the intervention; positive controls can help interpret negative results or detect expected effects. A separate no-treatment control may be unnecessary in some comparisons (e.g. different administration routes) or longitudinal within-subject designs. Pilot studies may not require controls. For clarity, identify test groups, comparators and controls clearly and explain any deviations (e.g. same control used across experiments). Diagrams are recommended for complex designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: The experimental unit (1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The experimental unit (e.g. a single animal, litter, or cage of animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the biological entity independently allocated to treatments (unit of randomisation). Experimental units may be individual animals, cages, litters, parts of an animal, or an animal over a time period (within-subject designs). Hierarchical organisation (cells within animals, animals within cages) affects unit definition. Do not conflate subsamples or repeated measurements with experimental units (avoid pseudoreplication). If subsamples are used, average them or use nested analysis; report clearly which entity is considered n. Clearly indicate the experimental unit for each experiment so sample sizes and statistical analyses can be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size (2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the exact number of experimental units allocated to each group and the total number in each experiment; indicate total number of animals used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report n per group and total per experiment (including independent replications). If the experimental unit is not the animal, also report number of animals to clarify the design. Differences between starting sample size and analysed n should be explained (see Inclusion and exclusion criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify exact numbers (2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the exact number of experimental units allocated to each group, and the total number in each experiment. Also indicate the total number of animals used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact n values (not percentages) for each group and experiment, including independent replications. If some animals were re-used across experiments, report that. Clarify animal counts when experimental unit differs from animal (e.g. cages as units).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how sample size was decided (2b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the sample size was decided. Provide details of any a priori sample size calculation, if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hypothesis-testing experiments justify sample size (a priori power/sample size calculation): state analysis method, predefined biologically relevant effect size (with justification), estimate of variability (and how estimated), chosen power and significance level, and directionality (one- or two-sided). Aim for appropriate power (commonly 80–95%). Use suitable calculators/software and consult a statistician for complex designs. If no power calculation was used, state this and justify the chosen sample size; for pilot/operational studies a priori calculations may be inappropriate—explain purpose and reasoning. Consider anticipated attrition when deciding sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any criteria used for including or excluding animals (or experimental units) during the experiment, and data points during the analysis. Specify if these criteria were established a priori. If no criteria were set, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define eligibility/disqualification criteria before data collection where possible. Inclusion criteria relate to eligibility during the study (distinct from animal characteristics); exclusion criteria cover technical issues, welfare endpoints, quality-control failures, outliers, etc. Decide and document criteria (ideally in a preregistered protocol). Report whether criteria were set a priori and include humane endpoint criteria when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report exclusions and reasons (3b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experimental group, report any animals, experimental units, or data points not included in the analysis and explain why. If there were no exclusions, state so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full accounting for exclusions/attrition and reasons (e.g. wrong treatment, toxicity, unrelated illness, sampling error, equipment failure, data-entry error). Explain handling of outliers and missing data and whether exclusion decisions were made blinded to group allocation. Use flowcharts or tables to summarise attrition per group. Describe methods used to explore and account for missing data; disclose use of built-in outlier removal tools if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact n for each analysis (3c)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each analysis, report the exact value of n in each experimental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute numbers (e.g. 10/20, not percentages) for animals analysed per outcome and time point. For repeated measures indicate which animals underwent which measurements at which times. Ensure all animals and data used in analyses are accounted for unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation (4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether and how randomisation was used to allocate experimental units to groups and to minimise confounding/bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the method of randomisation (e.g. simple, block, stratified), what was randomised (animals, cages, litters), any factors used for blocking or stratification, and who generated the allocation sequence. State steps taken to conceal allocation where applicable. If randomisation was not used, provide rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether and how blinding (masking) was used during allocation, conduct, outcome assessment and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate who was blinded (investigators conducting interventions, caretakers, outcome assessors, statisticians), stages where blinding was applied, and methods used to maintain blinding. If blinding was not feasible, explain why and report measures taken to minimize bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures (6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define outcome measures (primary and secondary) and how and when they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the primary outcome measure that addresses the main objective/hypothesis. Describe measurement methods, units, time points, and any blinding of outcome assessment. Justify choice of outcomes and their biological relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods (7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe statistical methods used for each analysis, including software, tests, assumptions and how data met those assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify statistical tests, model details, handling of repeated measures or hierarchical data, methods for multiple comparisons, how assumptions were checked, treatment of missing data, and software (with version). For complex designs report model formulas and covariates used and whether data transformations were applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals (8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed information on the animals used: species, strain, sex, age/weight, source, genetic status, and any other relevant characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report animal provenance, breeders/suppliers, health status, genetic modifications, numbers per sex, and any prior procedures or housing that could affect outcomes. Include justification for choice of species/strain and sex, and whether both sexes were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures (9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient details of all procedures so they can be replicated: what was done, how, where and when, and by whom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include doses, routes, timing, equipment and protocols used, peri-procedural care (anesthesia, analgesia), and welfare-related procedures. Describe acclimation, habituation, and standard operating procedures; reference detailed protocols or provide them in supplementary material or protocol repositories when lengthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results (10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the results for all outcome measures, with measures of variability and effect size where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide summary statistics (means/medians, variability measures such as SD/SE/CI), exact p-values, effect sizes with confidence intervals, and the n used for each result. Present data so readers can assess magnitude and precision of effects (figures/tables, individual data points where feasible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary in the abstract that includes key elements of the study (design, methods, main findings, and relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise information on study design, species/model, sample sizes, primary outcomes and main conclusions. Ensure abstract does not overstate findings and reflects primary objectives and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background (12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the study, including relevant literature and gap the study addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why the study is important, how it builds on previous work, and its intended contribution. Provide context on biological relevance and translational potential where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (13)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific objectives or hypotheses of the study, and prespecified primary outcome(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify primary and secondary objectives/hypotheses and their relationship to outcome measures. Use prespecification to guide sample size calculations and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement (14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an ethical statement describing approval by relevant bodies and compliance with welfare regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the name of the approving committee or authority, protocol or licence numbers, and statements on compliance with national/institutional animal welfare regulations and guidelines. Describe steps taken to minimize pain and distress and justify any procedures with potential welfare impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry (15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe housing, husbandry and environmental conditions that could affect the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report housing type, bedding, light/dark cycle, temperature, humidity, enrichment, group sizes, feeding and water access, and any special husbandry procedures. Note any deviations from standard conditions and their potential impact on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring (16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe monitoring and care of animals during the study, including humane endpoints and criteria for intervention/euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report monitoring frequency, clinical scoring systems, criteria for intervention or euthanasia, analgesia and perioperative care. Explain how welfare concerns were managed and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/scientific implications (17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the interpretation of the results and their scientific implications, including limitations and alternative explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider internal validity (bias, confounding), limitations of the model, reproducibility, and the strength of evidence. Avoid overstating conclusions; relate findings to prior work and discuss implications for further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/translation (18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability of the findings to other species, models, or contexts, and potential for translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider species/strain differences, experimental conditions, and biological plausibility when extrapolating to other systems or humans. State limitations to generalisability and requirements for further validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration (19)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the study protocol was preregistered or made available, and where it can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registration identifiers or links to registered protocols or Registered Reports. Preregistration of hypotheses, methods and analysis plans improves transparency and reduces selective reporting; report adherence to the preregistered plan and any deviations with rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access (20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement describing if and where study data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether data and metadata are publicly available, and provide repository names and persistent identifiers (DOIs). Follow FAIR principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable). Use domain-specific repositories (NCBI, EBI) where possible, or general repositories (Figshare, Dryad, Zenodo, OSF). Include sufficient annotation to enable replication and reuse; comply with publisher/funder data-sharing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests (21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any potential conflicts of interest, including financial and non-financial. If none exist, state this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose financial, non-financial, institutional and personal interests that could be perceived as influencing the research (employment, advisory roles, intellectual property, funding, ideology). Be transparent about perceived as well as real conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: List funding sources and funder role (21b)
rubrics_metrics.description: List all funding sources (including grant identifier) and the role of the funder(s) in the design, analysis, and reporting of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all financial supporters and grant numbers, including internal or employer support. State whether funders influenced study design, data collection, analysis, decision to publish, or manuscript preparation. If research was unfunded but performed as part of employment, name the employer.
